title: PowerShell encoding guard on the Windows spawn paths (+ an optional, separately-gated `powershell` tool)
wave: Wave 7 (TUI and Windows — the cuttable tail)
one_line: When omp spawns a real PowerShell to run a command, it now forces UTF-8 output with a guarded assignment so non-ASCII tool results stop coming back as mojibake — and a separate `powershell` tool is only built if the user says omp wants one.
user_visible_effect: A Windows user who points omp's `shellPath` at `pwsh`/`powershell` and runs commands through the `!` hotkey, the interactive PTY, or an ACP client terminal gets correctly-decoded non-ASCII output (paths with accents, CJK filenames, emoji) instead of mojibake. On POSIX hosts and on the default embedded-shell path nothing changes at all. If the user answers the scope question with yes, a `powershell` tool also appears in the tool list; if no, nothing appears.

steps.instruction: Get the scope answer before writing any code. Ask the user open question 4a verbatim: does omp want a first-class `powershell` tool, or is bash-only-on-Windows a deliberate scope decision? Record the answer in the PR description. Do NOT infer it from the codebase — the plan is explicit that this must come from the user. If the answer is NO or unanswered, do steps 1-6 only and skip steps 7-10 entirely; the item still lands.

Create `packages/coding-agent/src/exec/powershell-encoding.ts` exporting the exact prefix constant `try { [Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8 } catch {}` followed by a newline, and the pure function `withPowerShellUtf8Output(command: string, shell: string): string` that returns `command` unchanged when `isPowerShell(shell)` is false and `POWERSHELL_UTF8_PREFIX + command` when true. Import `isPowerShell` from `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils/procmgr` as a top-level named import. Do NOT re-implement the basename check — `isPowerShell` is the sanctioned central helper and duplicating it is a rule violation.

In `packages/coding-agent/src/exec/bash-executor.ts`, add `isPowerShell` to the existing procmgr import on line 17, then change `buildUserShellCommand` (line 379) so the `command` argument is transformed with `withPowerShellUtf8Output(command, shell)` before it is quoted and joined. Do not change its signature and do not move the call — `finalCommand` at :531-534 is the only caller and already routes exactly the shells that need this.

In `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/bash.ts`, change the body of `wrapShellLineForClientTerminal` so the incoming `line` is passed through `withPowerShellUtf8Output(line, shellConfig.shell)` before the `shellConfig.prefix` join. Add a top-level import of the helper. This is the ACP client-terminal path and it is currently the one spawn route with no encoding handling.

Confirm you did NOT touch the embedded-shell path. `executeBash` runs commands in brush-core (a POSIX shell engine in the native addon), not a spawned shell, so the default bash-tool path must not receive a PowerShell statement. Verify the only two edits are the ones in steps 3 and 4 — `git diff --stat` should list exactly two source files.

Write `packages/coding-agent/test/tools/powershell.test.ts` covering the three contracts in `test_contract` below, then build the native addon (`bun --cwd=packages/natives run build`) before running it — without the addon the module graph fails to load and the test errors out rather than failing an assertion. Run `bun run check:ts` and the test file. Both must pass.

W14b ONLY (answer was YES). Add an optional `shellConfig?: ShellConfig` field to `BashExecutorOptions` (the interface at lines 33-67) so a tool can point the executor at a specific shell, and have `executeBash` prefer it over `settings.getShellConfig()` at line 487-490. This is the seam the plan assumed already existed; it does not.

W14b ONLY. Create `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/powershell.ts` with a `PowerShellTool` class extending `AgentTool`, mirroring `BashTool` (bash.ts:473) for approval, streaming updates, and result details, delegating execution to `executeBash` with the pwsh `ShellConfig` from step 7. Set `readonly name = "powershell"` and `readonly label = "PowerShell"` following the convention at bash.ts:474 and :567. Port the approval gate correctly: `BashTool.approval` extracts compound-command segments only when `isPosixShell(shell)` (bash.ts:484), and `isPosixShell("pwsh")` is false, so PowerShell commands are matched as a whole chain — verify this against a real PowerShell rather than assuming it is right.

W14b ONLY. Create `packages/coding-agent/src/prompts/tools/powershell.md` and import it exactly the way `bash.ts:38` imports the bash description (`import powershellDescription from "../prompts/tools/powershell.md" with { type: "text" }`). Prompts are never built in code.

W14b ONLY. Register the tool: add `"powershell"` to `BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES` in `builtin-names.ts` and the factory entry in `BUILTIN_TOOLS` in `tools/index.ts`. Both edits are required in the same change or the `Record<BuiltinToolName, ToolFactory>` annotation will not typecheck. Re-run `bun run check:ts`.

test_contract: Three contracts, all asserting the value a consumer actually reads — the PowerShell interpreter parses the emitted command string, so its exact bytes are the contract (AGENTS.md: 'exact bytes/shape MAY be asserted when a provider, parser, protocol, or persisted consumer reads them'). (1) NEGATIVE/PRECEDENCE: for shells `/bin/bash`, `/bin/zsh`, and `cmd.exe`, `withPowerShellUtf8Output` returns the input byte-identical. This is the assertion that stops the item from being a rubber stamp — without it a helper that prefixes unconditionally would pass the PowerShell tests while corrupting every POSIX command, since a PowerShell statement is a syntax error in bash. (2) TRANSFORMATION: for `pwsh`, `powershell.exe`, and `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe`, the result starts with `try { [Console]::OutputEncoding=[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8 } catch {}` followed by a newline, and the user's command appears verbatim after it — this is the encoding contract the whole item exists to buy. (3) NON-CATASTROPHIC FAILURE: the guard is a `try`/`catch` block, so if the encoding assignment throws on an old host, the user's command is still reached. Assert the user's command appears AFTER the closing `catch {}` rather than inside it, i.e. the emitted line is a guarded statement followed by a separate statement. If the try/catch were dropped, or the prefix lost its `catch`, this test goes red. This is the honest POSIX-host proxy for the plan's 'assert the command still executes on a host where the assignment throws' — it defends the same contract without stubbing bytes and without a Windows host. What a consumer sees on regression: on Windows, every non-ASCII tool result renders as `ÄÆá»ç`-style mojibake, or the whole command aborts with a red error and no output.
gate: Two parts, and both must be run. (1) `bun run check:ts` — passes at HEAD today (measured: all 15 packages `Done`, no errors), so any type error introduced by this change turns it red. (2) `bun --cwd=packages/natives run build && bun test packages/coding-agent/test/tools/powershell.test.ts` — the test file must report 0 fail. The build step is mandatory and not optional: at HEAD the addon is absent, so any test whose module graph reaches `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` fails to LOAD. This is measured, not assumed: `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/tools/` currently gives 145 pass / 177 fail / 174 errors across 322 tests, and every one of the failures is the `Failed to load pi_natives native addon for darwin-arm64` error. Note that `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/bash.ts:19` imports `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils/procmgr`, whose line 3 imports `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` — so a test importing the tool (rather than only the pure helper) is unrunnable until the addon exists. The gate also includes a diff-scope check: `git diff --stat` must show exactly two production files (bash-executor.ts, bash.ts) plus the new helper and test — a third production file means the embedded-shell path was edited, which must not happen.
effort: W14a (the encoding guard, the part that lands unconditionally): S — roughly 30 production lines plus one test file. W14b (the separate `powershell` tool, only if open question 4a is answered yes): M, roughly 250-400 lines, because it needs a new `shellConfig` override seam on `BashExecutorOptions` and a new tool class — NOT the plan's 'S / ~80 dòng'. See plan_corrections #1: that 80-line figure is a pi-ref-shaped number and does not transfer to omp.
risk: The single most likely way to get this wrong is to believe the plan's 'Effort đã chốt, không còn mở ... đây là một tool definition cộng đăng ký, không phải một refactor' and drop pi-ref's 67-line `powershell.ts` into `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/`. It will not compile: `createShellToolDefinition`, `ShellToolConfig`, `createLocalShellOperations`, `BashOperations` and `BashSpawnHook` do not exist anywhere in omp's `tools/` module graph — `git grep` for the first two returns zero hits repo-wide, and the only copies of the latter three are in `extensibility/legacy-pi-coding-agent-shim.ts`, a legacy plugin-compatibility shim that is not the live tool. The tempting fallback is to fork `BashTool` (1504 lines), which is precisely the refactor the plan warns against. The honest smaller path is W14a: fix the encoding on the two spawn sites that exist, and treat the separate tool as its own scoped decision.
open_questions: Open question 4a (plan P3, lines 3072-3080) is unresolved and blocks W14b: does omp want a first-class `powershell` tool, or is bash-only-on-Windows a deliberate scope decision? This must be answered by the user, not inferred. Until it is answered, land W14a alone — the plan itself says W14 is droppable without losing any correctness anyone can observe today.

Given the brush-core finding below, the user should also be told that the mojibake the plan describes does NOT occur on omp's default Windows path. If they read the plan's 'mọi tool result non-ASCII bị hỏng' as a live bug report, that expectation needs correcting before anyone spends a day on W14b.

Should W14a ship at all if the answer to 4a is 'Windows support is deliberately bash-only'? It is ~30 lines and defends a real encoding contract on the spawn paths that DO exist (`!` hotkey, PTY, ACP terminal when `shellPath` is set to pwsh), so the recommendation is yes — but it is the user's call, since it is a behaviour change on a path they may not support.

pi-ref's version wraps the prefix inside the `exec` operations seam. The port above wraps at the command-composition site instead. If the user later wants the `powershell` tool, the W14a helper is reusable as-is; confirm no one objects to it living in `exec/` rather than `tools/`.

W14a is scoped to exactly those paths, which is why it is small.

plan_corrections.claim: omp already has PowerShell plumbing in the shell layer, implying only a thin tool is missing (implied by plan lines 1751-1755 and 1785-1787)
plan_corrections.verdict: PARTIALLY TRUE, and it is the useful half
plan_corrections.correction: omp's `procmgr` does already model PowerShell: `isPowerShell` (line 71) recognizes powershell/powershell.exe/pwsh/pwsh.exe, and `getShellArgs` (line 53) already returns `-NoLogo -Command` for it. So a user can already configure `shellPath: pwsh` and get correct spawn args. What is missing is only the encoding guard — which is why W14a is ~30 lines rather than a refactor. omp also already knows the encoding idiom: `utils/clipboard.ts:270` sets `[Console]::OutputEncoding = [Text.Encoding]::UTF8` (without a try/catch, in a `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'` script — a different context, so it is not a counterexample to the plan's try/catch requirement, but it is prior art for the pattern).
